promote_jobdef_note: SELF-PROMOTION, identical reasoning to the Databento chain (see futures_eod_databento.json) because it is the SAME shared silver jobdef: leviathan-dev-futures-eod-silver is DIGEST-PINNED in terraform (modules/batch/main.tf, var.futures_eod_image_digest) while the default promote runner leviathan-dev-silver-publisher-runner tracks the worker repo's floating :latest, so the shared-runner promote re-derives silver with a different build than the shadow it promotes. THE EXPOSURE IS LARGER HERE, not smaller: this chain promotes FOUR tasks and the free venues are exactly the legs whose dependency (xlrd, for JSE and the CEPEA archive) fails silently. The 2026-08-01 databento promote is the demonstrated failure (13/15 certified, then exit 1 on ZR/OJ under an older image's mode-blind row floor); this chain simply had not fired against a drifted runner yet. SAFE BY THE SAME PROOF EVERY FIRE: jobRoleArn=silver-publisher (glue:CreatePartition + kms:Sign) and all four --source producers run on this jobdef in the silver phase minutes earlier. ARMING: the rendered promote jobdef reaches the scheduler only through infra/terraform/envs/dev/dag_schedules.auto.tfvars.json (hand-authored, co-tenant discipline) -- regenerating _rendered/ does NOT re-arm the fire.
gate_baseline_uri_note: PER-SCHEDULE BY DECISION, and this SUPERSEDES the W1.0 seed. The rolling-census machinery is per-SCHEDULE (advance_rolling_census advances one baseline per fire, and a shared baseline would make each schedule's --diff read the other schedule's rows as unexplained drift), so silver_futures_eod carries one baseline per schedule: futures_eod_free (this one, four free venues) and futures_eod_databento. The family-level seed named in plan D6 and in jobs/audit/advance_rolling_census.py -- s3://leviathan-dev-shahem-001/cascade_census/rolling/futures_eod/census.json -- is SUPERSEDED and MUST NOT be consulted, minted or advanced; a diff against it would compare this schedule's rows to the union of both. futures_eod_gate.py gate 8 emits one silver_rebuild_gate command per schedule against its own baseline, deliberately.
chain_shape: fetch(czce|jse|cepea|miax incremental + euronext browser day-capture)->silver(one --source pass each, registered per leviathan_slug/trade_year)
euronext_capture_window_note: THE CAPTURE WINDOW, AND WHY 22:30Z IS INSIDE IT IN BOTH HALVES OF THE YEAR. The rendered live.euronext.com quote table publishes a Time column and NO DATE anywhere in its DOM, so trade_date comes from the raw key's as_of_date= segment and from nowhere else (transforms/raw_to_bronze/euronext_eod.py, point 1), and fetch_euronext_eod.py derives that default from datetime.now(timezone.utc).date(). The window is therefore a UTC statement, not the CET-local one D-PR-23 wrote down: the capture must sit AFTER the settlement publish and BEFORE 00:00Z. The publish is ~18:30 Paris = 16:30Z under CEST and 17:30Z under CET; 22:30Z clears it by 5-6 hours and sits 90 minutes before UTC midnight, in summer AND in winter. The earlier reading -- 'a 22:30Z fire is 00:30 CEST, i.e. after local midnight' -- measured the wrong midnight: the key's date rolls at 00:00Z, so a 22:30Z Wednesday fire lands Wednesday's session under as_of_date=Wednesday. D-PR-24 (user-ratified 2026-08-05, 'arm MATIF') also resolves the SETTL. semantics that D-PR-23 held this leg behind: the evening scrape reads the SAME session's settlement, so there is no T-1 risk and settle_kind='settlement' stands as CONTRACT_MAP pins it. THE RESIDUAL SEAM, stated rather than hidden: retry.maximum_event_age_in_seconds is 86400, so a retried fire may execute after 00:00Z and land the session under the NEXT UTC date -- silently, because this is the one leg with no independent date authority to cross-check. Every other venue in this chain reads its session date from inside the payload (JSE) or from a venue-chosen key segment (CZCE, MIAX). Narrowing this chain's event age, or teaching the producer to derive --as-of-date from <aws.scheduler.scheduled-time>, is the durable fix and is NOT carried here.
notes: ONE DESCRIPTOR, FOUR FREE VENUES, ONE CRON AT THE LATEST OF THEM. The plan (W1a D4) allowed either one descriptor per timezone or one at the latest publication time; this is the latter, and the reason is operational rather than aesthetic: the four legs share one table, one contract, one partition scheme and one gate, so four schedules would mean four censuses diffing against each other's rows as unexplained drift (the family-vs-schedule baseline question). CRON 22:30 UTC MON-FRI covers every venue's SAME-DAY publication: CZCE post-15:00 CST = 07:00 UTC, JSE post-close SAST = ~15:00 UTC, MIAX settlement ~14:35 CT = ~19:35 UTC, CEPEA ~18:00 BRT = ~21:00 UTC. 22:30 sits after the last of them with 90 minutes of margin, and deliberately NOT at 23:00, which is the yfinance futures_prices chain's slot. MON-FRI because no venue in this set holds a weekend session; a Monday session is published in the Monday fire, unlike the Databento chain's TUE-SAT next-morning pattern (that chain waits for FINAL settlements published the following day; these four publish their own final numbers same-day). WAVE 3 + retrofit_landed: a NEW class-A registered-partition chain, not part of the frozen wave-2 CLASS-B retrofit set. FAMILY is futures_eod, never futures -- dag_catalog maps silver_futures_eod to its own family and the silver_futures prefix would swallow the live yfinance table. Incremental windows are --lookback-days rather than a templated date because the scheduler substitutes only <aws.scheduler.*> context attributes. FOUR SEPARATE SILVER TASKS, one per --source, rather than one task with four sources: each stages its own (leviathan_slug, trade_year) partitions, so one venue's bad day fails one task instead of blocking the other three, and the manifests carry per-source job labels (futures_eod_czce / _jse / _cepea / _miax). JSE's fetch takes no --lookback-days ON PURPOSE: the portal object is overwritten daily and has no history, so its own --mode backfill raises NotImplementedError per plan gate 8, and a missed fire is permanently lost data -- this is the leg whose cadence discipline matters most. CEPEA's fetch takes no window either: the widget serves the last value only. PROMOTE_MODE IS stop_and_notify, NOT autonomous, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Nothing has been published canonically on this table yet, the row floors are PROVISIONAL until probe P10 recalibrates them against the CZCE ~2,600-day backfill (--row-floor report is what P10 uses), and the MIAX floor rests on a single observation. stop_and_notify renders promote.tasks EMPTY, so the machine publishes SHADOW only and a human promotes. SEQUENCING, and this is the trap: leviathan.silver.freshness computes lag from the newest CANONICAL-prefix object mtime and a shadow publish deliberately never resets that clock, so flipping this chain to autonomous must happen BEFORE the futures_eod family's freshness alarm is applied -- otherwise the alarm (treat_missing_data=breaching) pages the shared topic daily. BEFORE ARMING: (a) mint the gate_baseline_uri census (it does not exist yet), (b) register leviathan-dev-futures-eod-free-fetch in terraform (leviathan-dev-futures-eod-silver is shared with the Databento chain), (c) confirm the worker image carries xlrd -- JSE and the CEPEA archive both need it and the task preflights it per source; note xlrd>=2.0 is a CORE pyproject dependency rather than a [batch] extra, so unlike the Databento chain's databento pin NO rebuild is owed for it, (d) add the dag_schedules.auto.tfvars.json entry, which is what actually arms the fire. NO SECRETS: every one of these four venues is an unauthenticated public GET, so these jobdefs need no secrets/valueFrom block at all. ARMED 2026-07-29 (user-approved, explicit): promote_mode flipped stop_and_notify -> autonomous. The preconditions the stop_and_notify paragraph names are MET: every leg published canonically by hand (free: czce 34,164 / miax 1,554 / cepea 12,922 incl. the filled 1996-2026 series / jse 18; databento: 15/15 W2), union gates PASS, and the CZCE row floors held across the whole 2,628-file backfill (P10-czce closed). The stop_and_notify rationale above is retained as history. EURONEXT/MATIF ADDED 2026-08-05 (D-PR-24, user-ratified 'arm MATIF, smoke the exact command before first fire'), which makes this FIVE free venues, not four -- every count and enumeration above predates it and is left verbatim as the record of the W1a/W1b chain. Read 'four' as 'the four W1a/W1b venues' throughout; the NO SECRETS clause holds for the fifth too, because the Euronext product page is an unauthenticated public GET with no WAF (the browser is needed for CLIENT-SIDE RENDERING, not for access). WHAT IS DIFFERENT ABOUT THE FIFTH LEG, and it is one thing: its capture cannot run on leviathan-dev-futures-eod-free-fetch. The quote table is decrypted and rendered by the page's own JS out of an AES {ct,iv,s} blob, so table#future-prices-table exists only in a browser DOM; the producer drives headless Chromium and lands the table's outerHTML, and PLAYWRIGHT + CHROMIUM ARE NOT IN THE WORKER IMAGE. The capture task therefore rides leviathan-dev-browser-runner (docker/leviathan_browser, ENTRYPOINT ['python'], same script-form command convention), which is the jobdef the three 2026-08-04/05 matif-probe-* jobs ran this producer on successfully. Its SILVER task is the ordinary shared one: raw -> bronze -> silver happens inside jobs/batch/futures_eod_task.py on leviathan-dev-futures-eod-silver exactly as the other four do, so the self-promotion override still names the ONE jobdef every shadow_canonical publisher in this descriptor runs on. The fetch command takes NO window and NO --mode, like CEPEA's: the page serves TODAY and nothing earlier, --skip-existing is the default (a re-run costs no browser launch), and all three products (EBM-DPAR milling wheat, EMA-DPAR corn, ECO-DPAR rapeseed) are captured in ONE Chromium session. ALL THREE PRODUCTS ARE ARMED, and the completeness guard is what makes that legal rather than optimistic: each product's ready check WAITS for its own MEASURED expiry count before capturing (EURONEXT_MIN_ROWS: EBM 12, EMA 10, ECO 10, counted live 2026-07-29 from one capture per product), the capture sniff refuses a short tbody, build_bronze refuses a short or empty parse, and the per-day silver floor is 24 against a measured 32 -- deliberately set so that losing ANY ONE of the three products (which takes the day to 20-22) REDS the leg, because three independent page renders in one run is the real failure mode. Only EBM has a checked-in fixture (tests/fixtures/w1c/euronext_ebm_table.html) and only EBM carried the SETTL. semantics probe; EMA and ECO are armed on the strength of the identical table id and identical 12-column thead the live 2026-07-29 session measured, with those four guards as the fence. THREE HARD-FAIL SURFACES PER FIRE is the accepted cost, and its runbook is the one D-PR-23 asked for in advance: a legitimate venue DELISTING of an expiry reds this leg until a human re-counts the rendered table and re-pins EURONEXT_MIN_ROWS -- that is a code change by design and the floor is never lowered to make a capture pass. FRESHNESS CANNOT SEE A MATIF-ONLY STALL: silver_freshness_slas['futures_eod'] is family-level and the other four legs keep the clock fresh; per-leg granularity is D-EI-12 / R7's and is not forked here. THE SERVING FLIP IS STILL SEPARATE AND STILL DEFERRED: no MATIF slug has a PRICE_COVERAGE_START entry, so every MATIF lookup keeps returning status='declined' with its verbatim scope_note before any SQL compiles, and these rows land where nothing reads them until that entry is added in its own reviewed change. BEFORE THE FIRST FIRE: (a) smoke-test the EXACT rendered capture command on leviathan-dev-browser-runner / leviathan-dev-queue-ondemand, (b) adopt leviathan-dev-browser-runner into terraform WITH retryStrategy and attemptDurationSeconds (it exists at revision 1, untracked, with both null) in the post-freeze batch, (c) re-render dag_schedules.auto.tfvars.json, which is what actually arms the fire.
